proxy_language: Proto-Samic (with Proto-Uralic / Proto-Finno-Samic as deeper background); Komsa is a Final Palaeolithic–Early Mesolithic (c. 10,000–8,000 BP) coastal hunter-fisher culture of Finnmark, whose actual language is unknown and probably not Uralic
proxy_rationale: The Komsa people (Finnmark, N Norway, post-glacial coastal settlement) left no linguistic evidence. Their language is unrecoverable and may well have been unrelated to any later language; Uralic is generally thought to have arrived in the region much later. Proto-Samic (Sammallahti 1998; Aikio's work on Saami substrate and the 'Palaeo-Laplandic' pre-Uralic substrate) is the most defensible regional proxy because it is the earliest reconstructable language of the area and preserves layers of non-Uralic, non-Indo-European substrate vocabulary for fauna, landscape, and coastal terms. This is an evocative regional proxy only, not a claim of descent.
phonology: Proto-Samic (Sammallahti/Aikio notation). Vowels: *a *e *i *o *u *ā *ē *ī *ō *ū plus the central/reduced vowel *ë and diphthongs such as *ea *ie *uo *oa in later Samic. Consonants: stops *p *t *k *c (affricate, written c) *č; *s *š *ś *h *v *j; nasals *m *n *ń *ŋ; liquids *l *r; geminates and consonant clusters in medial position; consonant gradation (strong/weak grade) is a defining Samic feature affecting stems. Stress on the first syllable.
phonotactics: Native roots are typically disyllabic (C)V(C)CV, i.e. stems of the shape CVCV, CVCCV, CVCVC with a medial single consonant or a cluster/geminate, ending in a vowel (*-ë, *-a, *-e, *-i) in the proto-form; word-final consonants were limited (*-k, *-n, *-m, *-s, *-t in later stages). Initial consonant clusters are absent in native words. Vowel harmony of Uralic stems is reflected in backness patterns (a/o/u vs e/i). Medial clusters like -kt-, -st-, -lk-, -rt-, -ŋk-, -mp- are common.
orthography: Latin transliteration in scholarly Samic style: c and č for affricates, š, ž, ŋ, đ only in modern Northern Samic; proto-forms use ē ō ā for long vowels and ë for the reduced vowel. For game names use plain, readable Latin without diacritics except optional macrons: a e i o u plus ā ē ī ō ū, consonants p t k c s š h v j m n ŋ l r. Avoid b d g f z q x w y (foreign to Proto-Samic phonology).
morphology: Agglutinative, suffixing. Noun stems vowel-final; plural *-t (Samic nom. pl. -t), genitive/accusative *-n, illative/locative cases (*-s locative, *-k lative, *-j- in diphthongal stems). Derivational suffixes: *-ja/-jē (agent noun, 'one who does'), *-s/-ŋ (nominalizers), *-ne/-nē (diminutive or place), *-lē (instrument/ place), *-ta, *-ma (nominalization). Verbs: first-person *-m, third *-j, infinitive *-t; verbal derivation with *-skē- (frequentative), *-t- (causative). No grammatical gender, no articles.
compounding: Head-final: modifier precedes head, with the modifier in a bare stem or genitive in *-n (e.g. Saami boazu-guolli 'reindeer meat'; mearra-guolli 'sea fish'). 'X of Y' = Y-n X (genitive Y, then X) or simple compound Y+X. Agent names: object + verbal stem + agent suffix (e.g. guolle-+ -jē 'fish-catcher'). Place names: noun + locative/'place' suffix, or noun + word for 'fjord/bay/island/hill' (Samic vuotna 'fjord', suolu 'island', čohkka 'peak').
noun_phrase_order: Modifier (adjective, genitive noun, numeral) precedes head noun; head-final compounds; no articles. A name such as 'Sea-Seal Camp' is Seal-modifier + Camp-head.

water (Proto-Uralic *wete; N Sami čáhci is a different word)

notes: Komsa is known only from stone tools and coastal sites in Finnmark; its language is genuinely unknown and may be pre-Uralic and unrelated to any later language, so all forms here are speculative Proto-Samic/Proto-Uralic-flavoured constructions rather than Komsa words. Several roots above are tagged uncertain in the glosses (the first entry '*ëkta' is a placeholder and should be discarded by the name builder). Names should be built in the Proto-Samic phonotactic style: disyllabic/trisyllabic, vowel-final, first-syllable stress, no initial clusters, head-final compounds with optional genitive -n. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word.
